oneOf.description: One JSON object per line.
The combined log format of Nginx and Apache, which log analyzers read.

AccessLogSettings.description:
The access log. A thread of its own writes the lines, so requests never wait for it; lines
that it cannot keep up with are dropped and counted.

path.description:
File that the lines are added to, relative to the configuration file; standard output
when not set. SIGUSR1 opens it again, after a tool such as logrotate moved it.

AdminSettings.description: The Admin API and the dashboard.

listen.description: Address of the Admin API and the dashboard.

token_file.description:
File holding the Admin API token, created with a random token on first start if missing.
A relative path is resolved against `storage.data_dir`.

Balance.description: How requests are spread over the targets of an upstream. Every way follows the weights.

oneOf.description: Each request goes to the next target in turn.
Each request goes to a target picked at random.

Each request goes to the target with the fewest requests in progress, relative to its
weight.

Requests with the same key, see `hash_key`, go to the same target, and adding or
removing a target moves few keys.

Certificate.description:
A certificate chain and its private key, read from PEM files. Relative paths are resolved
against the directory of the configuration file. The files are read again whenever the
configuration is applied, so that replaced files take effect on reload.

cert.description: PEM file with the certificate chain, leaf certificate first.

key.description: PEM file with the private key.

ConfigSettings.description: Where the dynamic settings come from.

source.description: Source of the dynamic settings: listeners, certificates and the other entity tables.

oneOf.description:
The database. Changes go through the Admin API or the dashboard and are kept as versions.
Dynamic settings in the configuration file are ignored.
The configuration file. Edit it and send SIGHUP to reload; the dashboard is read-only.
The IP address of the client.
The path and the query of the request, as sent.
The value of a request header.
The value of a cookie.

HeaderRules.description: Changes to the headers of a message, made in this order: `remove`, `set`, `add`.

add.description: Values to add after the ones the headers have.

set.description: Headers to set, replacing the values they have.

HealthCheck.description:
Active health checks: every target is probed at an interval, a target that fails gets no
requests until it passes again, and a new target is probed once before it gets any.

healthy.description: Probes in a row that an unhealthy target must pass to get requests again. Default: 2.

host.description:
`Host` header of the request of `"http"`, such as `"api.internal"`. Default: `tls.sni`
if set, otherwise the host name of the target or its IP address; with the port of the
target, unless it is 80, or 443 with TLS.

interval.description: Time between the probes of a target. Default: `"5s"`.

path.description: Path and query of the request of `"http"`. Default: `"/"`.

status.description: Statuses that pass, for `"http"`. Default: 200 to 399.

timeout.description: Longest wait for a probe, from connecting to the response header. Default: `"2s"`.

unhealthy.description: Probes in a row that a healthy target must fail to get no more requests. Default: 3.

HealthCheckKind.description: How a health check probes a target.

oneOf.description: A TCP connection, without TLS.

A `GET` request with the protocol and the TLS settings of the upstream; a status in
`status` passes.

HttpSettings.description: HTTP settings of a listener. Settings left out follow the defaults of the running Wormway.

h2c.description:
Accept HTTP/2 without TLS from clients that start with it (prior knowledge), next to
HTTP/1.1. Only for listeners without TLS: those agree on HTTP/2 during the handshake
(ALPN). Default: `false`.

keepalive_timeout.description:
How long a kept-alive HTTP/1.1 connection, or an idle HTTP/2 connection, may wait for its
next request before it is closed, rounded up to whole seconds. `"0s"` turns HTTP/1.1
keep-alive off and closes idle HTTP/2 connections after one second. Default: `"75s"`, as
in Nginx.

Listener.description: A set of addresses served with one protocol.

listen.description: Addresses to listen on, such as `["0.0.0.0:443"]`.

tls.description: TLS termination. Without it the listener serves plain TCP.

certificates.description:
Names of the certificates the listener can present. The host name the client sends (SNI)
picks the certificate whose names cover it; when several do, the one listed first.

unknown_sni.description:
What to do when the client sends a host name that no certificate covers, or none at all.
Default: `"default"`.

oneOf.description: Human-readable lines.
One JSON object per line.

access.description:
The access log, one line per request. Off when not set; `[log.access]` turns it on with
the defaults.

level.description:
Log filter in `tracing` directive syntax, such as `"info"` or
`"info,wormway_runtime=debug"`.

time_format.description:
How the logs write times, the access log included: a strftime pattern such as
`"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S%.3f"`. RFC 3339 when not set. The combined access log keeps the
layout of Nginx and only takes the time zone.

time_zone.description: The time zone of the times in the logs.

PassiveCheck.description:
Passive health checks, as in Nginx: a target whose requests fail `max_fails` times within
`fail_timeout` gets no requests for `fail_timeout`. Failing means that the connection, its
TLS, sending the request or waiting for the response header failed or ran out of time; a
response passes whatever its status.

fail_timeout.description: Time in which the failures count, and for which the target is out. Default: `"10s"`.

max_fails.description: Failures within `fail_timeout` that take a target out. Default: 1.

regex.description: Paths in which this regular expression finds a match; ^ and $ anchor it.

PathPattern.description: A path prefix such as "/api/", an exact path such as { exact = "/" }, or a regular expression such as { regex = "^/v[0-9]+/" }.

oneOf.description: HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, served by the gateway.

Redirect.description: An answer that sends the client elsewhere.

status.description:
Status code: 301 or 308 for a permanent move, 302, 303 or 307 for a temporary one; 307
and 308 keep the method and the body. Default: 302.

to.description:
Where to: a URL or a path. `{host}` stands for the host name of the request, without the
port, and `{uri}` for its path and query as sent, as in `"https://{host}{uri}"`.

body.description:
Body, empty by default. A body is sent as `text/plain; charset=utf-8` unless
`response_headers` set another `Content-Type`.

Rewrite.description:
Changes to the path of the requests sent to the upstream. They apply to the normalized path,
which is then encoded again; the query stays as it is.

add_prefix.description:
Added in front of the path, after `strip_prefix`, such as `/api`: `/users` becomes
`/api/users`.

strip_prefix.description:
Removed from the start of the path when the path starts with it, such as `/v1`: `/v1/users`
becomes `/users`.

access_log.description:
Write the requests of the route to the access log, when `log.access` turns it on.
Default: `true`.

compress.description:
Compress responses with gzip, Brotli or zstd, the first that the client accepts, when
their type is text-like. Streams of server-sent events and gRPC are left alone. Default:
`false`.

listeners.description: HTTP listeners whose requests the route sees. Without it, every HTTP listener.

match.description: Which requests the route takes. Without it, every request.

priority.description: Precedence over the other routes that match a request: higher first. Default: 0.

redirect.description:
A redirect to answer the requests with, such as
`{ to = "https://{host}{uri}", status = 301 }`.

request_headers.description:
Changes to the headers of the requests sent to the upstream. They come after the
`X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Real-IP` and `X-Request-Id` headers that Wormway sets, so they can
change or remove those too.

respond.description:
A fixed response to answer the requests with, such as
`{ status = 503, body = "down for maintenance" }`.

response_headers.description:
Changes to the headers of the responses, whether they come from the upstream or from the
route.

rewrite.description: Changes to the path of the requests sent to the upstream.

timeouts.description:
Time limits of the requests to the upstream, in place of those of the upstream, such as
`{ read = "5m" }` for slow reports.

RouteMatch.description:
Conditions on a request. A request matches when it meets every condition that is set.

Paths are compared after normalization: every `%XX` decoded, `.` and `..` segments resolved
and repeated slashes merged, so that `/a/../admin/` and `/admin%2F` both count as paths
under `/admin/`.

headers.description:
Conditions on headers, by name: a value that one of the values of the header must equal,
`true` for a header that must be present, or `false` for one that must be absent.

hosts.description:
Host names, such as `example.com`, or `*.example.com` for one label in front of
`example.com`. Without it, any host.

methods.description: Methods, such as `["GET", "HEAD"]`. Without it, any method.

paths.description:
Paths: a prefix such as `"/api/"`, an exact path such as `{ exact = "/" }`, or a regular
expression such as `{ regex = "^/v[0-9]+/" }`. Without it, any path.

RouteTimeouts.description: Time limits of a route, in place of those of its upstream.

read.description: Longest wait for the next data from the upstream. Default: `read` of the upstream.

write.description:
Longest wait for the upstream to take the next data of a request. Default: `write` of
the upstream.

shutdown_timeout.description:
How long open connections may take to finish when Wormway shuts down or their listener is
changed or removed. Connections still open after that are closed.

threads.description: Worker threads of the data plane. `0` starts one per CPU core.

StorageSettings.description: Where Wormway keeps its database and runtime state.

data_dir.description:
Directory for the database and runtime state. A relative path is resolved against the
directory of the configuration file.

weight.description: Share of the requests relative to the other targets.

Target.description: A server of an upstream: its address, such as "10.0.0.1:8080" or "api.internal:8080", or a table with a weight. Host names are resolved when the configuration is applied and every 30 seconds after.

TimeZone.description: The time zone of the times in the logs.

oneOf.description: Coordinated Universal Time.

The time zone of the system: the `TZ` environment variable, otherwise `/etc/localtime`.
Changes to either take effect within a second.

Timeouts.description:
Time limits of the connections and requests to the targets of an upstream. A request that
runs out of time is answered with 504.

connect.description: Time to connect to a target, TLS handshake included. Default: `"10s"`.

idle.description: How long an idle connection to a target is kept for the next request. Default: `"60s"`.

read.description:
Longest wait for the next data from a target, such as the response header. Default:
`"60s"`.

write.description: Longest wait for a target to take the next data of a request. Default: `"60s"`.

UnknownSni.description: Handling of a TLS handshake for a host name that no certificate of the listener covers.

oneOf.description:
Present the first certificate of the listener, as Nginx presents the certificate of its
default server.

Fail the handshake, so that the certificates are not shown to clients that do not know a
host name they cover, such as scanners connecting by IP address.

Upstream.description: A group of servers that requests are balanced over.

balance.description: How requests are spread over the targets. Default: `"round_robin"`.

hash_key.description:
What `consistent_hash` hashes. A request without it, such as one without the header,
hashes its client IP address instead. Default: `"client_ip"`.

health_check.description: Probe the targets at an interval and send requests only to those that pass.

passive.description:
Keep requests away for a while from targets whose requests fail. Off when not set;
`passive = {}` turns it on with the defaults.

protocol.description: The protocol spoken with the targets. Default: `"h1"`.

retries.description:
How many other targets a request tries when it cannot connect, from 0 to
[`Upstream::MAX_RETRIES`]. A request that reached a target is not sent to another one.
Default: 1.

targets.description: The servers. A server with weight 2 gets twice the share of one with weight 1.

timeouts.description: Time limits of the connections and requests to the targets.

tls.description:
Connect to the targets with TLS. `tls = {}` checks their certificates against the
system's certificate authorities.

UpstreamProtocol.description: The protocol spoken with the targets of an upstream.

oneOf.description: HTTP/1.1.
HTTP/2 over TLS, agreed on during the handshake; needs `tls`. gRPC needs HTTP/2.
HTTP/2 without TLS, from the first byte (prior knowledge); not with `tls`.

UpstreamTls.description:
TLS to the targets of an upstream. Relative paths are relative to the configuration file;
the files are read again on every change and on SIGHUP.

ca.description:
PEM file with the certificate authorities that the certificates of the targets must come
from, in place of the system's.

cert.description:
PEM file with the certificate chain, leaf first, that Wormway presents to targets that ask
for one. Set together with `key`.

key.description: PEM file with the private key of `cert`.

sni.description:
Name sent to the targets (SNI) and that their certificates must have. Default: the host
name of the target, or its IP address, which is checked against the IP addresses of the
certificate and not sent.

verify.description:
Check the certificates of the targets. `false` accepts any certificate, so that anyone
on the path can read and change the traffic. Default: `true`.

admin.description: The Admin API and the dashboard. Static: a restart applies changes.

certificates.description:
TLS certificates by name. Dynamic: read from this file only when `config.source` is
`"file"`.

config.description: Where the dynamic settings come from. Static: a restart applies changes.

listeners.description: Listeners by name. Dynamic: read from this file only when `config.source` is `"file"`.

log.description: Logging. Static: a restart applies changes.

routes.description:
Routes of the HTTP listeners by name. Dynamic: read from this file only when
`config.source` is `"file"`.

server.description: Process settings. Static: a restart applies changes.

storage.description: Where Wormway keeps its database and runtime state. Static: a restart applies changes.

upstreams.description: Upstreams by name. Dynamic: read from this file only when `config.source` is `"file"`.

version.description: Version of the configuration format. This build reads version 1.
